sections.heading: Teen and provisional licensing conditions
sections.markdown:
## Teen and provisional licensing conditions

FACT_ID: sec07-R01 | anchor: A01
The ordinary Class D application requires age 16 or older and a valid instructional permit held for one year and one day, together with the applicable REAL ID requirements. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=28]

FACT_ID: sec07-R02 | anchor: A01
To obtain Class D, arrange the road test, surrender CP or affirm that surrender is impossible, provide school evidence and awareness-program completion, obtain adult consent and pass the road test. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=28]

FACT_ID: sec07-R03 | anchor: A01
The Class D education course uses 30 classroom hours or equivalent online study, plus 6 certified on-road hours or the approved parent-teen driving guide. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=28]

FACT_ID: sec07-R04 | anchor: A01
Class D preparation includes at least 40 hours of other driving, with at least 6 hours at night. Completion of the approved parent-teen guide serves as an affidavit for that requirement. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=28]

FACT_ID: sec07-R05 | anchor: A01
When a certified instructor supplies the on-road course component, a separate confirming document is required at testing. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=28]

FACT_ID: sec07-R06 | anchor: A01
A teen with a parent on active United States military duty may use an out-of-state driver-education certificate when it is within 9 months of the sixteenth birthday. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=28]

FACT_ID: sec07-R07 | anchor: A01
A 17-year-old documenting military enlistment need not meet the usual one-year-and-one-day CP holding period and receives Class C after successfully completing the road test. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=28]

FACT_ID: sec07-R08 | anchor: A01
A Class D driver must not drive between midnight and 5 a.m.; the handbook gives no exception to this restriction. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=28]

FACT_ID: sec07-R09 | anchor: A01
Only immediate family may ride during the first 6 months of Class D. The handbook includes parents, stepparents, grandparents, siblings, stepsiblings, children and other household residents in that group. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=28]

FACT_ID: sec07-R10 | anchor: A01
During the second 6 months of Class D, at most 1 passenger younger than 21 may be outside the driver's immediate family. After the first year, that maximum becomes 3. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=28]

FACT_ID: sec07-R11 | anchor: A01
Class D progression to Class C requires no major-traffic-offense conviction causing mandatory suspension during the preceding 12 months. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=28]

FACT_ID: sec07-R12 | anchor: A01
A teen moving to Georgia without a valid license or permit from another state must meet the requirements for a Georgia resident's initial credential. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=28]

FACT_ID: sec07-R13 | anchor: A01
A teen with a valid out-of-state license or permit normally may seek a comparable Georgia document, but differing state requirements must be resolved with DDS. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=28]

FACT_ID: sec07-R14 | anchor: A01
The adult who signed a minor's credential application can request revocation before the eighteenth birthday using the department's designated form with a notarized signature. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=28]

FACT_ID: sec07-R15 | anchor: A01
For a driver younger than 21, the handbook lists suspension for hit-and-run, street racing, fleeing an officer, reckless or aggressive driving, and other offenses assessed at least 4 points. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=28]

FACT_ID: sec07-R16 | anchor: A01
The listed high-point teen offenses include unlawfully passing a school bus, improper passing on a hill or curve, and speeding at least 24 miles per hour above the limit. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=28]

FACT_ID: sec07-R17 | anchor: A01
A driver younger than 18 also faces suspension for accumulating at least 4 points within a 12-month period. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=28]

FACT_ID: sec07-R18 | anchor: A01
The handbook's limited-permit exception for the listed non-DUI teen suspension applies only to an applicant aged at least 18 whose conviction was for speeding from 24 through 33 miles per hour above the limit. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=28]

FACT_ID: sec07-R19 | anchor: A01
The teen DUI suspension summary states that no limited driving permit is available for the described first DUI suspension. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=28]

Misconceptions: The adult who can sign an application and the person allowed to supervise a CP driver have different minimum ages and requirements.
Mnemonic: Age, adult, evidence, education, experience, restrictions.
Glossary: Graduated licensing is progression through conditional credential stages; revocation at an adult signer's request requires the prescribed form.
Dynamic-fact isolation: Permit duration, military exceptions, points, suspension and limited-permit policy retain current legal review.
